subject: Derived-data boundary & DPA - Spectrum analytics carveout
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@spectrum.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@spectrum.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify DPA request re: derived outputs and analytics use

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to get explicit language in the DPA about how Spectrum can use model outputs for product analytics. The ask is narrow but important for our legal team:

- We need confirmation that non-personalized model outputs (aggregated/derived metrics from inference) may be stored and analyzed for product telemetry and feature usage metrics.
- We cannot grant rights for training Redwood models on customer data; training must be explicitly excluded.
- Subprocessor question: our analytics vendor (TelemetryAnalytics Inc.) will receive aggregated telemetry. Will that be allowed if Redwood lists them as a subprocessor?

I've attached a short PDF summarizing our requested carveout and a proposed mutual action plan timeline. Can you route this to the right person on your side (legal / security / product) and let us know what evidence you need? We’re targeting an NDA + DPA executed by end of next sprint.

Attachments: Spectrum_DPA_ask.pdf (1 page)

Thanks —
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Legal Ops, Spectrum AI
contracts@spectrum.ai

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@spectrum.ai>, contracts@spectrum.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify DPA request re: derived outputs and analytics use — need product/security signoff

Folks — forwarding Spectrum's ask. Key points: they want to allow storage/use of derived/aggregated model outputs for product analytics but explicitly exclude training. They will send aggregated telemetry to TelemetryAnalytics Inc. if we approve subprocessor.

Questions for Product/Security:
- Product: does our runtime or caching make "outputs" susceptible to inclusion of PII or model-context tokens that would make them sensitive? Need a clear definition we can put in contract: e.g., "derived, non-attributable metrics that do not include raw customer-provided text or PII."
- Security: what controls or evidence do we require on retention, access, and audit logging for exports to a telemetry subprocessor? Any redlines we should pre-approve?

Customer timeline: they want a signed DPA within ~2 weeks. I've added HubSpot link and the MAP in Drive. Please reply with suggested contract language or a short list of must-have guardrails so I can go back to Maria.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@spectrum.ai>, contracts@spectrum.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA request re: derived outputs and analytics use — redlines + questions

Thanks Logan — reviewed Spectrum's PDF. High-level position and proposed edits below (I attached a redlined draft).

1) Define "derived outputs" precisely: propose text — "Derived outputs are machine-generated results returned by Redwood's inference API that do not contain verbatim customer-supplied text, customer identifiers, or other data that can reasonably be attributed to an identified or identifiable natural person."

2) Training exclusion: add explicit clause: "Customer data and derived outputs shall not be used to train, improve, or fine-tune Redwood models without Customer's prior written consent."

3) Subprocessors & analytics vendors: allow analytics subprocessors subject to the following controls:
   - Redwood will maintain an approved subprocessor list; any addition requires notice and a 30-day objection window.
   - Telemetry exports must be pseudonymized/aggregated prior to transfer; no raw request/response pairs containing potential PII.

4) Retention & access: propose a maximum retention window for derived analytics of 90 days by default (customer can request shorter windows), with access logged and restricted to product and analytics teams.

5) Auditability: include right for Customer to request evidence of controls (SOC-type summary) and a requirement for Redwood to maintain audit logs for export events for at least 180 days.

Open items for Product/Sec input:
- Can Product guarantee that outputs can be pseudonymized automatically (i.e., we can strip any verbatim text before export)? If not, we need to tighten the clause and disallow exporters of raw outputs.
- Is 90-day retention reasonable from ops/feature needs?

I attached redlined_dpa_spectrum_v2.docx with inline edits. If Product can't support automated pseudonymization, recommend we push for a contractual prohibition on exporting raw output and accept aggregated metrics only. Security supports the audit/logging pieces and the 30-day subprocessor notice.

— Olga Petrov
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@spectrum.ai>, contracts@spectrum.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA request re: derived outputs and analytics use — proposed next steps

Quick update — Security concurs with Olga's proposed redlines. Two clarifications from Sec:

- Runtime exposure: Product to confirm whether the inference KV cache or any debug logs could contain verbatim customer content that would be included in exports. If so, exports must be scoped at the API layer to block raw results.
- Evidence: we'll provide a SOC-summary packet and an export-audit report template; knits to HubSpot MAP.

Recommended next steps (short):
1) Priyom: update the MAP with the redline milestones (I've put placeholders in MAP-Spectrum-SP4821.xlsx).
2) Product (Olga / Product eng): confirm whether we can pseudonymize outputs prior to export or whether we must contractually ban raw output exports.
3) Logan: respond to Spectrum by EOD Tuesday with the summary below and attach our redlined DPA.

Logan — suggested reply to Spectrum (short):
"Thanks — we've reviewed and propose the attached redline. We can permit aggregated, non-attributable analytics exports under the conditions in the redline (no training, 90d retention default, approved subprocessor list with notice). Product is verifying the technical export constraints and we'll share SOC-summary and an export-audit template. Can we schedule a 30-minute call on Tue to align?"

I can join the call if needed.

— Mina Haddad
Security Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
